text:
anya: quick heads-up — toggled the compile+cuda-graphs path in staging and saw throughput drop ~18% for the 2k token chat workload. Perf regression starts after ~5 requests per session, looks like a warmup/hand-off issue.

mike: ugh. which kernels are swapping? any nvprof/Nsight traces? :thinking_face: 

anya: attached flame was sparse but kernel table shows we go from fast_attn_f32 -> aten_cudnn_contraction at seqlen ~128->256 boundary. seems like autoselect pivot moved.

david: that pivot shift is suspicious. did autotuner record a new best for the 256 path? we recently changed the cost model to weight memory-bound kernels less.

anya: yes — autotune DB shows new preference for the cudnn-backed matmul at 256 even though latency on compiled graphs is worse. hypothesis: torch.compile produces slightly different op fusion layout which trips kernel heuristics.

sara: i've seen heuristics pick different kernels when KV cache shapes change mid-session. if compile emits static shapes, cudagraphs will bake in kernel choices and never re-evaluate. could be a stale decision.

anya: here's the minimal repro command I used on an a100: 

```bash
export RW_ENABLE_COMPILE=1
export RW_USE_CUDAGRAPHS=1
python perf_runner.py --model redwood/tiny --batch=1 --seq=2048 --querylen=128 --sessions=200
```

mike: can you repro with RW_AUTOTUNE_LOG=1 and attach the tune record? also try RW_FORCE_KERNEL=fused_attention to see if it narrows it down.

anya: will do. attaching autotune snippet: 

```
# autotune record excerpt
seqlen_bucket: 256
selected_kernel: cudnn_gemm_v1
measured_latency_ms: 0.98
predicted: 0.85
context: torch.compile + cudagraphs
```

david: predicted vs measured delta ~15% — that matches the end-user regression. i think the cost model is mis-estimating the fusion overhead introduced by torch.compile.

jen: any chance the KV cache alignment causes a different memory stride so the cuBLAS path loses L2 benef? we saw similar with NV small-warp fragmentation.

anya: interesting — stacktrace from the compiled path shows an extra reshape before the matmul. reshape likely elided in eager path so kernel footprints differ.

sara: propose we add a small change: when compile+cudagraphs are enabled, prefer kernels validated under compiled traces (i.e., require autotune sample runs under RW_ENABLE_COMPILE to update DB). fallback: add hysteresis so a kernel switch requires 2 consecutive sessions of better perf before flipping.

mike: +1. also add a tiny health-check: after a kernel switch, run N=5 synthetic requests at target seqlen to verify. if measured > predicted by X%, trigger rollback. Keeps production steady.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (1794023600): GPU util 92%, host CPU 18%, avg token latency 17.3ms -> 20.5ms after change, p50->p95 widened.

david: action items:
- anya to run autotune with compile flag and produce new records (anya)
- mike to add runtime gate/hysteresis + rollback probe (mike)
- sara to add doc note in runtime heuristics about compile/cudagraph interaction (sara)
- jen to validate memory-stride theory with small repro (jen)

anya: started autotune job now, will push logs to /opt/rw/profiling/1794023450.tar.gz when done.

mike: timeline? can we hotfix gating within today?

anya: i should have autotune samples in ~30m. if they confirm, mike can still add gate and we can roll a patch to staging tonight.

jen: quick thought — we could also add a cheap compiled-trace sampler during first N requests of a session to detect mismatch early. avoids full autotune but gives empirical measure.

sara: yeah that might be the sweet spot. small extra cost but prevents large regressions.

anya: OK will prioritize outputs. thanks all. :raised_hands:

mike: thanks — please ping when logs uploaded and i'll kick off a gate branch.

perf-bot: reminder: add test harness case for compile+cudagraphs in nightly perf suite to catch this automatically.

anya: noted. i'll add the test and link the PR.
